name: Cranial parasympathetic outflow
summary: The craniosacral parasympathetic system leaves the brainstem in four cranial nerves, each with its own brainstem nucleus and peripheral ganglion: the oculomotor nerve (Edinger–Westphal nucleus → ciliary ganglion) constricts the pupil and accommodates; the facial nerve (superior salivatory nucleus → pterygopalatine and submandibular ganglia) drives lacrimation, nasal secretion and submandibular and sublingual salivation; the glossopharyngeal nerve (inferior salivatory nucleus → otic ganglion) drives the parotid; and the vagus (dorsal motor nucleus and nucleus ambiguus → ganglia in the walls of the viscera) slows the heart, constricts the bronchi and drives gut secretion and motility down to the splenic flexure. Long preganglionic and short postganglionic fibers, acetylcholine at both synapses and muscarinic receptors at the target are its pharmacological fingerprints.

anatomy.location: Nuclei in the midbrain (Edinger–Westphal), pons (superior salivatory) and medulla (inferior salivatory, dorsal vagal, ambiguus); preganglionic fibers in CN III, VII, IX and X; ganglia in the orbit (ciliary), pterygopalatine fossa, submandibular region, below the foramen ovale (otic) and within the thoracic and abdominal viscera.

subdivisions.name: Oculomotor (III)
subdivisions.note: Edinger–Westphal → ciliary ganglion → sphincter pupillae, ciliary muscle

subdivisions.name: Facial (VII)
subdivisions.note: superior salivatory nucleus → greater petrosal nerve → pterygopalatine ganglion (lacrimal, nasal, palatine glands); chorda tympani → submandibular ganglion (submandibular, sublingual glands)

subdivisions.name: Glossopharyngeal (IX)
subdivisions.note: inferior salivatory nucleus → tympanic plexus, lesser petrosal nerve → otic ganglion → parotid via the auriculotemporal nerve

subdivisions.name: Vagus (X)
subdivisions.note: dorsal motor nucleus and ambiguus → cardiac, pulmonary, esophageal and abdominal plexuses → intramural ganglia

function: Rest-and-digest control of the head and thoracoabdominal viscera: pupillary constriction and accommodation, secretion of tears and saliva, cardiac slowing, bronchoconstriction, gut secretion and peristalsis.

bestView.label: dorsal vagal nucleus region in the medulla

imaging.normalAppearance: Nuclei and ganglia are not resolved on routine MRI; the relevant imaging is of the nerves along their courses (orbit for the ciliary ganglion region, temporal bone for the facial nerve, skull base for IX and X).

pathology.pathology: Compressive third nerve palsy with pupil involvement
pathology.finding: PComm aneurysm compressing the superficial parasympathetic fibers.

pathology.pathology: Facial nerve lesion proximal to the geniculate ganglion
pathology.finding: Enhancement of the labyrinthine segment with reduced tearing and salivation on that side.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Imaging of the relevant cranial nerve; pharmacological pupil tests; Schirmer test

lesionEffects.deficit: Dilated, unreactive pupil with loss of accommodation
lesionEffects.mechanism: Preganglionic fibers in CN III or the ciliary ganglion

lesionEffects.deficit: Dry eye and reduced nasal secretion
lesionEffects.mechanism: Greater petrosal nerve or pterygopalatine ganglion (facial nerve lesion at or above the geniculate ganglion)
Chorda tympani (VII) or otic ganglion pathway (IX)

examination: Pupil reaction to light and near; dilute pilocarpine test for denervation supersensitivity
Heart rate variability with breathing and Valsalva
pearls: The pupillary fibers travel on the surface of the third nerve: compression hits them first, ischemia spares them
A facial palsy with dry eye and loss of taste is proximal (geniculate or above); with normal tearing it is distal

latin: Pars parasympathica: nervi craniales III, VII, IX, X
